title: Project BIM Manager
purpose: Responsible for project-level information management and governance. Ensures information produced on the project is planned, structured, coordinated, validated, and delivered in accordance with TIVERIT BIM Standards, ISO 19650 principles, and agreed project information requirements. Operates as the ISO 19650 Information Management Function within a single project.
authority_statements: Approve project-level information planning artifacts (BEP, MIDP, TIDPs) for compliance
Enforce validation, coordination, and acceptance rules for project deliverables
Require corrective action when information does not meet declared requirements
May approve project coordination workflows and validation rules within enterprise constraints
May reject project practices that violate BIM governance or information management standards
May reject uncontrolled use of tools or automations that compromise information integrity
May not override enterprise BIM Standards (S1–S9) or BIM Director authority
May not override contractual obligations agreed by Project Director/Client
May not control commercial terms, budget, or scope
responsibilities: Own BEP authoring and updates at project level within enterprise templates
Define and maintain MIDP and TIDPs for the project's BIM deliveries
Design and oversee BIM coordination, validation, and acceptance workflows
Ensure correct and consistent use of CDE (e.g. ACC) as authoritative system of record
Establish LOD/LOI expectations and permitted-use boundaries for the project
Identify information-related risks early and drive corrective action
Escalate governance conflicts when delivery pressure threatens information quality
Provide transparency on BIM information readiness, risks, and dependencies to Project Leadership
accountabilities: Project-level information reliability and governance (not overall project success or production speed)
Ensuring information can be trusted for declared and permitted use
Fulfillment of ISO 19650 project-level Information Management Function
approvals: Model validation and acceptance evidence at project level
CDE project folder configurations and permissions models
Project-level deviations within permitted standards boundaries
inputs: Client EIR/AIR/PIR and contractual BIM requirements
Enterprise BIM Standards from BIM Director
Coordination logs and validation evidence from Project BIM Coordinator and BIM Detailer
outputs: CDE governance protocols and compliance reports
